summary: Apple starts testing AI on Chinese iPhones using Alibaba's Qwen, Tencent launches a new flagship model, and young shoppers build apps to talk themselves out of Double 11 buys.
body: Apple Intelligence, Apple's set of AI features, is finally coming to iPhones in mainland China. Testing for registered developers began on November 4, with a public launch planned for December with iOS 27.3[^1][^2]. Because AI services in China need government approval, Alibaba's Qwen model powers the features there, and cloud requests go to Alibaba's servers rather than Apple's[^1][^2]. China's internet regulator approved the launch in July; Tech Times reports that the approval test checks the model refuses prompts on about 2,000 banned topics, a detail we could not confirm elsewhere[^2].

Tencent released Hy4, its new flagship AI model, on November 4[^3][^4]. Early reports differ on one point: one calls it open-weight, meaning anyone can download and run it, while another quotes Tencent saying the weights will follow "in the coming days"[^3][^4]. Electric-car makers posted mixed October numbers: BYD delivered 483,125 cars and Xpeng a record 50,237, but the China Passenger Car Association estimates overall retail car sales fell sharply from a year earlier[^5][^6].

Daily life: ahead of Double 11 (November 11), China's biggest online shopping festival, dozens of small WeChat and Alipay apps now let users post what is in their cart so friends or strangers can vote on whether to buy it, Sixth Tone reports[^7]. One 20-year-old student who built such an app says it saved her over 80 yuan in a week[^7]. An Accenture report cited by Sixth Tone found 82% of China's Gen Z were saving or cutting non-essential spending[^7]. My read: careful spending by young people is one reason China's government finds it hard to boost consumption.
